subject: Control-domain topology snapshot and SOC2 evidence checklist
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenline.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Greenline SecOps <secops@greenline.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control-domain topology and SOC2 evidence request

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick responses earlier. We're prepping the SOC 2 scoping for Greenline and need a concise security architecture snapshot for Redwood's Private + Dedicated offering. Specifically can you provide: 

- A control-domain topology diagram that shows control-plane vs data-plane demarcation for both Dedicated and Private deployments (include any shared services and egress points).
- A short checklist of the artifacts you can supply for SOC 2 (network diagrams, segmentation legend, ACL/GW examples, routing summaries, sample audit logs).

Our timeline is tight — the SOC 2 scoping call is next Thursday (28th). If you can share a draft topology and checklist this week that would help our auditor baseline.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Security Operations
Greenline Systems
[Attachment: auditor-scope-2026.pdf]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenline.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-domain topology and SOC2 evidence request

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-draft control-domain topology (PDF) and a segmentation legend (SVG). The diagram intentionally separates: 

- Control plane (Redwood control plane, model management, orchestration) — logically isolated, runs in our control tenancy.
- Data plane (inference hosts) — dedicated GPU pools for Dedicated; private VPCs for Private with per-tenant routing.
- Shared services (auth, telemetry, metrics ingestion) — accessible via mTLS-protected service endpoints and explicit egress controls.

What I'm including in the checklist:
- control-domain-topology-v1.pdf (diagram w/legend)
- segmentation-legend-v2.svg (colors + label keys)
- sample-egress-acl.txt (redacted IP ranges)
- sample-audit-log-snapshot.json (example tokens removed)
- scope-matrix.xlsx (which artifacts we provide for Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

Notes and caveats: for Private deployments we show optional on-prem edges and customer-managed KMS. Our artifacts are redacted for customer identifiers; if Greenline requires raw logs or unredacted configs we will need a data access agreement.

I'm copying Kimberly for the routing/egress details and Marissa for SOC 2 packaging. If you want a short 30m call before Thursday we can do a walkthrough and lock scope.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | solutions@redwood.ai
[Attachments: control-domain-topology-v1.pdf, segmentation-legend-v2.svg, scope-matrix.xlsx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenline.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-domain topology and SOC2 evidence request

Grace / Ethan — quick clarifying items from the topology we attached: 

1) Egress points: the diagram shows two explicit egress classes (customer-managed egress for Private; Redwood egress for Dedicated/Hosted). Can you confirm which log formats Greenline's auditor needs (syslog vs JSON ingest)?

2) KMS: for Private we list optional bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) with HSM-backed keys. If Greenline plans BYOK, we'll need the key policy and trust boundaries to include in the evidence pack.

3) Cross-region routing: are you planning to include EU regions in scope? That changes our network ACL examples slightly.

Inline from Ethan's original request: 
> "...include any shared services and egress points."

Suggest we also include a short-runbook (one pager) describing how a tenant is onboarded to a Dedicated GPU pool and how network isolation is validated (automated tests + manual checklist). Grace — can you draft that runbook and drop it in the Drive link so Ethan's auditor can preview?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sample-egress-acl.txt]

From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greenline.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-domain topology and SOC2 evidence request

Grace / Kimberly — this is great, thanks. Confirming:

- Auditor wants JSON log samples (they consume ingest JSON), so the sample-audit-log we saw is perfect.
- We'll scope only US regions for this engagement (no EU).
- Greenline will not require BYOK for the first phase, so you can exclude raw key policy artifacts for now.

We'll take the diagrams as-is for the baseline. Please add the one-page onboard runbook you mentioned to the Drive folder and I'll share the Drive link with the auditor. Also good to set a 30m walkthrough for Wednesday (27th) at 10:00am PT if you and Marissa are available.

Thanks again — the attachments match what we need.

Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Security Operations, Greenline Systems
[Attachment: auditor-confirmation-2026.eml]
